reviewer_role_disclosure: Reviewer authored the shared teacher core; raw journal arithmetic is independently recalculated here without invoking the experiment runner or D4 analyzer.
decision_authority: Recommendation only; does not alter root scientific gate or original result files.
method_diagnosis: The registered smaller-step schedule does not fix the observed singleton-to-group mismatch or establish consistent main128 benefit. It repairs much of one late-sample failure while worsening the early and middle samples.

main128_summary.interpretation: Average improvement over the original schedule is dominated by the single late observation; it is not consistent across the three observations and still loses to static in the three-observation mean.

late_gripper.interpretation: At128 this sample improves substantially, including gripper error, but chunk3 retains a0.536804 normalized gripper deviation. cost.scope: Supplementary teacher diagnostic cost; not deployment latency. Main-run calls are reused as evidence and are not newly executed or added to this cost.

recommendations: Retain original G1 no-go; do not start full G2/G3 from these three observations.
Treat the preregistered smaller-step diagnostic as completed and inconclusive for a useful revised main128 method; do not continue unregistered step-size search on these same observations.
Preserve all budgets and the earlier late256 error spike alongside late128 recovery; do not report only the favorable endpoint.
limitations: Three observations from three different task/episode/phase combinations cannot disentangle task and phase or support suite-level inference.
Singleton sums are diagnostic additive approximations, not promised bounds; changing schedules also changes visited sets, so residual differences do not isolate a pure step-size effect.
The same BF16-derived actions and recorded versions are used; no cross-precision or new GPU replication was performed.
The remaining late gripper discrepancy is a normalized action deviation; this review did not evaluate postprocessing, environment execution or closed-loop success.
No test data, new labels, training or parameter tuning were used.
